body_html:
A motorbike trip through Vietnam can only be as long as the permission to be in the country. For travellers who enter on an e-visa, that ceiling comes from a handful of rules: how long the visa can last, how it relates to the passport, which border gates it allows and which exit date ends up stamped in the passport. This article sets out what official sources say about each point, with dates where the pages carry one and a note wherever the sources disagree.

Two limits apply from the start. The e-visa portal and FAQ do not cover riding licences or what a rental shop checks. Foreign-government advice cited below does touch on licences, and it is not uniform: the UK page says UK riders need a UK licence plus a 1968-convention International Driving Permit, while the Australian and Canadian pages say licences and permits issued in those countries are not accepted and a Vietnamese licence is required. This article does not settle that question; read the linked licence guide, check with the Vietnamese authorities or your own embassy, and remember that what a shop asks for is not the same as legal permission to ride. And Vietnam's national e-visa portal and its FAQ page show no date, so what follows reflects those pages as read on 24 October 2026. Fees and rules change, so confirm anything that matters on the official portal before relying on it.

What the e-visa allows

The table gathers the main figures and shows which publisher states each one.

ItemWhat the source saysPublisher
Maximum lengthThe visa cannot exceed 90 days under the lawVietnam e-visa FAQ (no date shown)
Passport marginE-visa validity must be at least 30 days shorter than the passport's validity. UK advice also says the passport needs an expiry date at least six months after arrival and two blank pages; check bothVietnam e-visa FAQ (no date shown); UK entry-requirements page (no date shown)
Entry type and feeSingle entry 25 USD, multiple entries 50 USDVietnam e-visa portal (no date shown); the U.S. Mission page gives the same figures
If the visa is refusedThe application fee is paid through the portal's e-payment gateway and is not refundedVietnam e-visa portal (no date shown)
Application windowUp to one year before the planned entryVietnam e-visa FAQ (no date shown)
Who can applyForeigners who wish to enter Vietnam, not those currently residing thereVietnam e-visa FAQ (no date shown)

The FAQ's wording on who can apply points to requesting the visa after leaving Vietnam. The UK government makes a related point: an e-visa obtained while in Vietnam only starts once the holder exits the country and re-enters. The portal also warns that its official addresses are evisa.gov.vn and thithucdientu.gov.vn, and that unofficial pages may lead to unauthorised fees.

The 90-day ceiling and a long ride

For anyone planning a long ride, 90 days is the outer limit of what the visa itself can cover. The sources give no processing times and no step-by-step method for extending an e-visa. Smartraveller says Vietnam does not issue automatic extensions, that extensions are only possible before the visa expires, and that the passport needs at least six months' validity left when applying for an extension; the UK, US and Australian pages direct readers to Vietnamese immigration authorities. For long road trips, the UK safety-and-security page warns that visiting villages, communes or wards close to the border may need permission from the provincial police.

A sensible way to plan, offered here as advice rather than as a rule, is to start from the exit date and work backwards. A rental that ends comfortably before the last permitted day leaves slack for delays. Distance terms also matter on a long trip, and Rental Motorbike Mileage Limits: Read the Odometer Clause Before a Long Trip covers reading the odometer clause before setting off.

Entry and exit points

Vietnam's e-visa portal says foreigners using e-visas must enter and leave through international border gates designated by the Government. The U.S. Embassy page adds that the designated gates include all international airports. The sources vary on how many gates exist, so this article gives no count; the portal's own list is the one to read.

The sources do not fully agree on how far the e-visa limits the gates you may use:

  • The e-visa FAQ says foreigners using an electronic visa are not required to leave through the same border gate where they entered.
  • The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office says e-visas restrict travellers to the entry and exit points selected on the application. Its entry requirements page shows no date.
  • The Government of Canada, in travel advice last updated 19 October 2026, says the e-visa allows entry only through the port named in the visa approval notice.

Because the sources differ, the safest course is to follow the entry and exit points shown on the approval notice, and to check the official portal if a plan involves a different exit, such as flying out of another city after a road trip.

Check the exit date at the border

Australia's Smartraveller advice, updated on 24 September 2026, says the passport is stamped on arrival with the date by which the traveller must leave Vietnam. It tells travellers to check that the expiry date written in the passport is correct before leaving immigration or border control, because it may differ from the date shown on the visa. For a rider, that stamped date is the one a rental should be planned to finish well before.

The UK government's entry requirements page, undated as noted above, warns that overstaying a visa can mean being stopped from leaving until a fine is paid, followed by possible deportation and a ban on visiting Vietnam in the future.

Documents to carry while travelling

Among the obligations the e-visa portal lists for foreigners is carrying a passport or international travel document, along with any documents relating to residence in Vietnam, when travelling, and presenting them when competent authorities ask. The UK government's safety and security advice, on a sub-page with no date of its own, says visitors must always carry photographic ID and that the authorities will accept a printed copy of the photo page of the passport and of the visa.

That UK line is advice to British travellers. Neither it nor the portal says which document a rental shop will ask for, so it is worth asking the shop before arriving. The UK safety page also says not to use a passport as a deposit for hiring vehicles or as a guarantee. Licences for riding are outside what the e-visa pages cover; Vietnam Driving Licence Classes A1 and A Explained for Motorbike Renters Under the 2025 Rules explains the licence classes for motorbike renters.

Digital Pre-Arrival Form

Smartraveller says people entering through international airports such as Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi and Phu Quoc are encouraged to complete a Digital Pre-Arrival Form online within 72 hours of arrival. The Government of Canada says completing a digital arrival form is not mandatory, but warns that this could change and could expand to other airports at short notice. Check both the official portal and the traveller's own government advice shortly before departure.

Before booking the bike

Visa rules can change, so the official portal is the place to confirm the points above before any rental dates are fixed. The booking side is a separate task, and Hanoi Motorbike Rental Guide: What to Check Before Booking sets out what to check before booking.

Sources checked

  • Immigration Department, Ministry of Public Security, Viet Nam National Electronic Visa system homepage: application fee payment, border gates and foreigners' obligations (no date shown). https://evisa.gov.vn/
  • Immigration Department, Ministry of Public Security, e-visa FAQs: validity, passport margin, application window, exit gates (no date shown). https://evisa.gov.vn/faq
  • UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, entry requirements for Vietnam: entry and exit points, e-visa started while in Vietnam, overstaying (no date shown). https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/vietnam/entry-requirements
  • U.S. Mission Vietnam, visas and entry or exit: e-visa fees and designated gates (no date shown). https://vn.usembassy.gov/vietnamese-visas-and-entry-exit/
  • Government of Canada, Vietnam travel advice: port of entry on the e-visa and the digital arrival form (last updated 19 October 2026). https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/vietnam
  • Australian Government Smartraveller, Vietnam: exit-date stamp and the Digital Pre-Arrival Form (updated 24 September 2026). https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/asia/vietnam
  • UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, safety and security in Vietnam: carrying photographic ID (no date shown). https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/vietnam/safety-and-security
